text: What was the Lahore Resolution? It was a March 1940 resolution of the All-India Muslim League that called for grouping Muslim-majority regions into independent states with autonomous constituent units.
Who moved the Lahore Resolution? A. K. Fazlul Huq of Bengal formally moved the resolution at the Lahore session.

How is the Lahore Resolution connected to Pakistan and partition? The text did not name Pakistan directly, but it became a major constitutional and political turning point that fed later partition outcomes.
Why is the Lahore Resolution important in Bengal politics? It elevated Bengal's role in late-colonial representation politics and sharpened debates on autonomy, identity, and statehood.
The Lahore Resolution turned Bengal from a provincial arena into a central author of partition-era constitutional politics.
